marks.gloss_en: תא שמע: מכל האוכל אשר יאכל -- food that came in water is susceptible, food that did not is not; so what is susceptible only by regard for sanctity does not count
'of all food that may be eaten [on which water comes]' (Lev 11:34) -- food that came in water is rendered susceptible, food that did not come in water is not
אטו ריש לקיש לית ליה אוכל הבא במים? -- he knows that rule; his question is whether regard for sanctity is like food that came in water
ומאי בואו ונסמוך על דברי רבי שמעון? לרבי שמעון לא מכשיר, לרבי חייא מכשיר!
בנתקנח מיהו אשוו להדדי -- where wiped off, neither renders; Rebbi is one, and one's words do not stand against two
Rebbi is one, and the words of one do not stand in the place of two
ומאי בואו ונסמוך על דברי רבי שמעון? לרבי שמעון לא מכשיר, לרבי חייא ספיקא!
לענין שריפה מיהו שוו להדדי -- neither burns; Rebbi is one ...; והכי קאמר: כגון זאת תולין, לא אוכלין ולא שורפין (Steinsaltz: this is what R' Chiyya means)
'and drinks the blood of the slain' -- to exclude spurting blood, which does not render seeds susceptible
one slaughtered and splashed blood on a gourd -- Rebbi: it is rendered susceptible
R' Oshaya: on whom shall we rely? let us rely on the words of R' Shimon
Rav Pappa: all agree that where the blood is on it from beginning to end, it renders susceptible
R' Chiyya holds: slaughter exists only at the end, and this is blood of a wound
Rav Ashi: 'one suspends' means forever -- neither eat nor burn
Reish Lakish asks: the dry portion of meal-offering flour -- does one count first and second [degree impurity] in it, or not?
